defects.description: handle() remembers handled deliveries by deliveryTag, which the broker assigns per delivery, so a redelivered payment event is added to the balance again.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import {PaymentConsumer} from "./src/consumer.js"; import {Ledger} from "./src/ledger.js"; const l=new Ledger(); const c=new PaymentConsumer(l); const e={id:"p1",account:"acme",amount:30}; await c.handle({deliveryTag:1,event:e}); await c.handle({deliveryTag:2,event:e}); console.log(await l.read("acme"));'

defects.why_missed: Every test sends each payment once; the broker's redelivery of one event with a new tag never happens in the suite.

defects.description: handle() reads the balance and writes it back across two awaits with nothing ordering deliveries to one account, so two payments handled at the same time lose one of them.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import {PaymentConsumer} from "./src/consumer.js"; import {Ledger} from "./src/ledger.js"; const l=new Ledger(); const c=new PaymentConsumer(l); await Promise.all([c.handle({deliveryTag:1,event:{id:"p1",account:"acme",amount:30}}), c.handle({deliveryTag:2,event:{id:"p2",account:"acme",amount:12}})]); console.log(await l.read("acme"));'

defects.why_missed: The suite awaits each delivery before sending the next, so no two handles ever overlap.
